summary: Compose native body and Coulomb kernels in Rust TGS frame order with on-device body parameter derivation.
regressions: Eleven composed frame fixtures cover empty/free motion, contact impact, friction, stacks, 31/33/65/129-column widths, interleaved batches, center-of-mass offsets, scaled worlds, zero PGS count and warmstart scaling.
Ten body-parameter fixtures cover zero timestep/iteration count, native MAX_FLT and adjacent values, scales and gravity copies.
Independent fixed-body checks guard against accidentally treating Rust default unit mass properties as static; free-motion checkpoints check semi-implicit gravity analytically.
Frame validators reject overlapping velocity writers, mismatched uniform/schedule fields, invalid buckets/capacities, recycled links and out-of-contract split slots.
differences: No Rust physics changes; all expected states execute production Rust entry points with mutable-reference noalias disabled.
This is a composed frame from supplied manifolds and fixed colors, not a collision-generating or changing-topology simulation backend.
Body coefficient packing runs on the device. Every dependent frame stage uses resident native buffers and synchronous dispatch boundaries.
Existing floating tolerances and zero-distance numerical block remain; Ascend source lowering does not claim vendor compilation or device execution.
